notes: 27 products: Banquet 5, Healthy Choice 4, Marie Callender's 4, Hungry-Man 2, P.F. Chang's 3, Birds Eye 3, Orville Redenbacher's 3, Act II 1, Green Giant 2. Categories: frozen_tray 15, steam_bag 5, pouch 1, popcorn_bag 4, oven_only 2.

Source was SmartLabel (smartlabel.labelinsight.com) via WebFetch for 26 of 27 records; direct curl to that host is blocked by the agent proxy. WebFetch gave intermittent SERVER_ERROR on some IDs (18859101, 5041968, 9423889, 6444367, 6729662 instructions; 12573547 and 12155417 nutrition on two tries). Those Marie Callender's records have null nutrition.
For a few pages (zw-105, zw-114, zw-119, zw-121, zw-122) the fetch tool paraphrased the label text instead of quoting it. Times and temperatures were kept, but step wording should be re-checked.

No SmartLabel page states tray, bowl or bag material or a resin code, so container.material and recycling_code are null for all records. Every Banquet, Marie Callender's and Hungry-Man tray in this batch has microwave and conventional oven directions for the same tray (350 or 375°F, often with the film left on), so they are flagged 'inferred CPET (oven-safe tray)'. Healthy Choice Power Bowls and Steamers say do not cook in conventional or toaster ovens, so their containers are microwave-only and get no CPET inference.

The only Conagra tray-material statements found are from 2009 (30 to 40 percent post-consumer recycled plastic in nearly all Healthy Choice, Banquet, Kid Cuisine and Marie Callender's trays, a dual-ovenable monolayer rPET design). The March 2022 Citizenship release gives a company-wide figure (about 93 percent of packaging by volume renewable, recyclable or compostable) with no per-tray detail. Current tray resin still needs package photos.

Popcorn: labels give no wattage, only a time range on HIGH plus 'stop when popping slows' and 'Do NOT use popcorn button'. These are marked partial under the schema rule. The app needs a separate rule for popcorn (listen-based stop, no popcorn button). Conagra told IPEN it removed PFAS from US Act II packaging in 2022; no statement for Orville Redenbacher's bags was found.
Act II is not on SmartLabel; its record comes from a Conagra Foodservice case listing, so it has no UPC and a garbled net-weight field.

P.F. Chang's Home Menu single-serve rice and noodle bowls, Bertolli, Evol and Gardein were not found on SmartLabel, and the Ahold retailer sites (Hannaford, Stop & Shop, Giant, Food Lion) that list them were in maintenance. The P.F. Chang's items on SmartLabel were a brown rice pouch, a fried rice steam bag and a stovetop-only skillet meal, and those three were used.

New negative examples: Green Giant Garlic Parmesan Crispy Smashed Potatoes ('Microwave oven not recommended', oven only) and P.F. Chang's Chicken Fried Rice skillet meal (stovetop only, no microwave directions and no explicit prohibition, so do_not_microwave is null).

Wattage patterns hold from batch 1. Conagra trays, bowls, Power Blend bags and P.F. Chang's bags use a single 1100 W reference. Birds Eye plain vegetable Steamfresh uses a 1200/1000/800 W table with stovetop below 800 W. Green Giant uses a 1200/1000/700 W table.
Multipacks (Healthy Choice 3-packs, Birds Eye 4-packs) carry their own UPCs. Net weight is the carton total and directions are per meal or bag. Single-unit UPCs were not collected.

Spare candidates read but not included: Orville Redenbacher's Kettle Corn Value Size 12 Classic Bags (SmartLabel 8890061, UPC 027000523827, 1.5-2.5 min HIGH, 3.28 oz bags), and Marie Callender's Fettuccini With Chicken & Broccoli 4 Meals (5047710, UPC 021131504724), left out because zw-004 is the same product. SmartLabel IDs 6095538 and 6890764 are Orville kettle and stovetop popping kits with no microwave directions.

packaging_statements.statement: Conagra put 'between 30 percent and 40 percent post-consumer recycled plastic in nearly all of the frozen meal trays' for these brands. The article adds that 'most frozen meals trays used by other companies are made of crystallized PET plastic'. The page is undated; the transition began 'in June' (2009 per related coverage).

packaging_statements.brand: Conagra (frozen entrees and meals, brands not named)
packaging_statements.statement: Tray described as the 'first application of monolayer rPET for a dual-ovenable package in North America', with rPET 'qualified at 40% of the food tray's total content'. Stated goal was to build infrastructure to 'collect and reprocess CPET trays'. Dated 3 Oct 2009.

About 93% of packaging materials by volume were renewable, recyclable or compostable (estimate partly based on industry average weights). Goal: 100% of current plastic packaging renewable, recyclable or compostable by 2025. Release dated 17 Mar 2022. No tray, bag or popcorn detail.

Conagra email of 10 Feb 2023, quoted in the IPEN report (March 2023): 'We removed PFAS last year from the packaging used for our ACT II microwave popcorn products in the U.S.' An Act II bag bought in Indonesia (sample IDN-PA-23, Mar 2022) tested positive for PFBA, PFHxA, PFHpA, FHET and 6:2 diPAP. The report says PFAS are used because they form a grease-repelling chemical barrier on the bag paper.
